stories.title: IIM Bangalore earns IGBC platinum green campus certification
stories.summary: IIM Bangalore has become the first educational institution in India to receive the Indian Green Building Council’s Platinum certification for its campus. The rating system acknowledges the institute’s commitment to energy efficiency, water conservation, and sustainable operations. The campus was originally designed by architect B.V. Doshi.

stories.summary: The institute becomes India’s first educational institution to receive Platinum status under IGBC Green Campus Rating System Version 1.0, supported by wastewater recycling, 350 kWp solar capacity and sustainable campus operations. stories.summary: Bengaluru, Nov 16: IIM Bangalore has achieved the prestigious Platinum certification under the Indian Green Building Council’s Green Campus Rating System, Version 1.0, becoming the first educational institution in India to receive this distinction under the rating framework. The certification recognizes IIMB’s integrated approach to sustainable campus development, encompassing energy

stories.title: Finance gaps persist at UN climate summit in Antalya
stories.summary: Discussions at the UN climate summit in Antalya have highlighted the divide between ambitious climate goals and the funding required to achieve them. While new initiatives aim to assist with project preparation, negotiators remain at odds over public finance and the transition away from fossil fuels.

stories.title: Climate movement takes its fight beyond emissions at Türkiye summit
stories.summary: Thousands of activists, workers and indigenous groups took to Antalya’s streets, turning a rainy day into a vibrant demonstration for climate justice during the ongoing climate conference. - The protesters challenged fossil fuel dependence, corporate control of natural resources, forest destruction and the growing inequalities of climate change. - Their

stories.title: Salt Lake City tightens developer tax rebate rules
stories.summary: The Community Reinvestment Agency board has voted to reduce the maximum tax reimbursement for developers from 90 percent to 80 percent. Projects must now also meet mandatory sustainability and public art policies. The council voted unanimously to approve the changes to its reimbursement programs.

stories.title: TCC Group calls for global calcined clay alliance at COP31
stories.summary: TCC Group Holdings is advocating for a global Calcined Clay Transition Alliance at COP31 to accelerate the adoption of low-carbon cement. The company’s subsidiary, CIMPOR, expects to produce 1.5 million tonnes of calcined clay annually by the end of 2026, targeting a reduction in CO2 emissions.

stories.title: India’s net-zero transition requires significant foreign investment
stories.summary: A report by economist Nicki Hutley suggests India’s 2070 net-zero goal presents a 22.7 trillion dollar investment opportunity. While domestic resources could cover 70 percent of the transition, the country faces a 6.5 trillion dollar funding gap that will require support from foreign investors and development banks.

stories.title: M3M and Jacob & Co announce luxury residences in Gurugram
stories.summary: M3M India has partnered with watchmaker Jacob & Co. for a 1,650-crore residential project in Gurugram. The development, located on the Dwarka Expressway, will feature 120 luxury units. The company expects the project to generate a total revenue of 3,300 crore.

stories.title: Delhi government moves toward single-agency infrastructure model
stories.summary: The Delhi government plans to consolidate infrastructure project stages under a single consultancy arrangement to improve coordination. The Delhi State Industrial and Infrastructure Development Corporation has invited expressions of interest for architects and engineers to manage projects from initial conceptualisation through to the final handover.

stories.title: Knight Frank report highlights office retrofitting potential
stories.summary: Retrofitting India’s ageing office buildings could unlock 3.76 lakh crore in value, according to Knight Frank India. The report suggests that such upgrades could increase asset values by 76 percent. The National Capital Region and Mumbai lead the country in potential volume and value appreciation.

stories.title: Architect Hafeez Contractor to design new NSE headquarters
stories.summary: Architect Hafeez Contractor has been selected to design the proposed National Stock Exchange headquarters in Mumbai’s Bandra Kurla Complex. The project, unveiled in November 2026, adds to the architect’s portfolio of commercial and public infrastructure. Contractor began his career five decades ago with a monthly salary of 30 rupees.

stories.title: Monterey Peninsula College opens new welcome center
stories.summary: Monterey Peninsula College has opened a 14,500-square-foot welcome center to replace an outdated facility. The new building serves as a campus gateway, housing support services, social lounges, and meditation rooms. ABA Studios designed the project, which was managed by Brailsford and Dunlavey.

stories.title: This 35,000-square-foot manor in Gujarat unfolds around a sacred courtyard
stories.summary: Seated on a two-acre clearing within a larger twenty-acre estate of dense mango orchards and limestone formations, this manor in Gujarat, designed by AR13, an AD PRO Directory partner, quietly enters into a gracious dialogue with the terrain. Classical grandeur meets regional roots through a design grounded in Vastu principles.

stories.title: New residential facility at the National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bangalore by DCOOP Architects
stories.summary: The seven-acre expansion at NLSIU, Bangalore is planned as a residential precinct, accommodating approximately 2,000 students across eight residential blocks, together with 90 housing units for staff and faculty. Responding to the site’s topography, the master plan steps the residential blocks along the terrain, allowing the landscape to remain a

stories.title: Mumbai Metro 2B project targets March 2027 completion
stories.summary: The Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority is working to launch the Andheri West-Saraswat Nagar stretch of Metro Line 2B by March 2027. Civil and systems work is 75 percent complete, with contractors currently installing the final girders at the congested Juhu Circle.

stories.title: Bhumika Realty expands retail footprint in Faridabad
stories.summary: Bhumika Realty has leased 1 lakh square feet of retail space at its development in Faridabad. The latest round of leasing included 45,000 square feet, with tenants such as Bikanervala and Jetts Fitness. The developer aims to lease an additional 1 lakh square feet by March 2027.

stories.title: MVRDV designs Skanderbeg-shaped tower in Tirana
stories.summary: The 85-meter Skanderbeg Building in Tirana is designed to resemble the country's national hero, Gjergj Kastrioti Skanderbeg. The structure uses the site's maximum buildable volume to form a bust, with the building's edges forming shoulders and the head turned toward the square. Architecture is now literal.

stories.title: Isern Serra completes Circl pilates studio in Barcelona
stories.summary: Design practice Isern Serra has opened Circl, a 180-square-meter fitness studio and matcha cafe in Barcelona. The project aims to combine the worlds of pilates and matcha, which the firm claims share a common philosophy of wellbeing and balance. The two worlds meet below street level.

stories.title: Tato Architects creates open space in Akashi house
stories.summary: Tato Architects has completed a 136-square-meter house in Akashi. The firm describes the design process using a football analogy, noting that it is essential to create room for teammates to play. The architects concluded that what mattered most for the house was creating open space.

stories.title: Nikken Sekkei stacks public spaces in Hangzhou
stories.summary: Nikken Sekkei has completed the HaloPlaza mixed-use complex in Hangzhou. The design stacks offices, retail, and apartments above a revitalized canal, with elevated open spaces connected by atrium voids. The firm describes the composition as a way to stack buildings like second and third ground planes.

stories.title: Daichi Silent River Tree Sauna wins Dezeen award
stories.summary: The Daichi Silent River Tree Sauna has been named the 2026 architecture project of the year. The biophilic project, which punctures its framework with surrounding woodland, also won the leisure and wellness category. The judges praised the project for its integration with the forest.

stories.title: IndexBox reports growth in carbon-negative materials
stories.summary: The global market for carbon-negative building materials is entering a high-growth phase. According to an IndexBox report, the construction sector is pivoting from emission reduction to active atmospheric carbon removal. Materials include biochar-based insulation, hempcrete, carbon-cured concrete, and mycelium composites.

stories.title: Cornetta Arquitetura completes Pinhal House
stories.summary: Cornetta Arquitetura has completed the 690-square-meter Pinhal House in the Mantiqueira Mountains. The firm describes the project as a rare union between architectural ambition and conservation. The house is situated in the heart of the mountain range.

stories.title: Natura Futura completes floating center in Ecuador
stories.summary: Natura Futura has finished The Floating Cultural Center in Ecuador. The project aims to reconnect the river with the city while reclaiming its memory. The architects state the center is designed to foster new forms of coexistence and collective development for the local community.

stories.title: SO Arquitetura completes Black Timber project
stories.summary: SO Arquitetura and Design has completed the 160-square-meter Black Timber project. The architects describe the work as an elementary operation that uses a single material to explore two opposing conditions. The building was completed in 2026.

stories.title: MoMA awards prize to Dhaka-based URBANA
stories.summary: The Museum of Modern Art has awarded its first Ambasz-MoMA prize to Kashef Chowdhury/URBANA for the Friendship Centre in Bangladesh. The prize, described by the museum as the largest award for a single architecture project, recognizes work that repairs architecture's relationship with nature.

stories.title: Architecture Dialogue builds temporary sales pavilion in Chennai
stories.summary: Architecture Dialogue has completed the 2,500-square-meter Baashyaam Experience Centre in Chennai. Designed as a temporary marketing pavilion, the project aimed to rethink the conventional sales office as an immersive experience. A primary requirement for the project was speed and reversibility.

stories.title: Cross-laminated timber market growth projected
stories.summary: The cross-laminated timber market grew from $1.9 billion in 2025 to $2.25 billion. The sector is projected to maintain an 18.1 percent compound annual growth rate until 2030 as the construction industry increases its use of engineered wood solutions. Momentum is currently being experienced.

stories.title: Cross-laminated timber market forecast to reach $6.2 billion
stories.summary: The global cross-laminated timber market is expected to reach $6.2 billion by 2033. The industry is moving beyond specialist timber construction into larger commercial and institutional projects. Adoption remains dependent on building codes, manufacturing capacity, and the availability of low-carbon materials.

stories.title: Construction adhesives market faces structural transformation
stories.summary: The global market for construction adhesives and sealants is entering a decade of structural transformation through 2035. According to IndexBox, sustainability mandates and infrastructure renewal are reshaping demand for chemical formulations. Procurement behavior is described as more disciplined as the market enters 2026.

stories.title: Autoclaved aerated concrete market expands
stories.summary: The autoclaved aerated concrete market is seeing momentum driven by construction sector growth and material innovations. As sustainability becomes a critical consideration for developers, the material is emerging as a preferred choice. The industry is currently experiencing a period of steady expansion.

stories.title: Researchers develop rammed material from crushed brick
stories.summary: Researchers have developed a rammed material composed of recycled crushed brick waste. The material, termed Crushed Brick Rammed Material, serves as a soil-free alternative to traditional cement-stabilized rammed earth. It aims to maximize the use of construction and demolition waste in urban renewal projects.

stories.title: Renishaw on the repeat purchase of metal 3D printers
stories.summary: Renishaw is discussing the factors that lead manufacturers to invest in a second metal 3D printer. Hydraulic valve manufacturer Domin purchased a four-laser RenAM 500Q in 2023, followed by a 500Q Ultra a year later. The primary challenge remains how to produce enough valves.

stories.title: All Time Plastics opens bamboo board facility in Assam
stories.summary: All Time Plastics Limited has commenced operations at its new engineered bamboo board manufacturing facility in Madanpur, Assam. The unit, operated by subsidiary All Time Bamboo Private Limited, occupies 75,700 square feet and has an installed production capacity of 3,000 cubic metres of board per annum.

stories.title: All Time Plastics shares move on Assam facility news
stories.summary: Shares of All Time Plastics traded at Rs 203.00 following the announcement of its new bamboo board facility in Assam. The stock, which has a face value of Rs 2, reached a 52-week high of Rs 299.00 in November 2025 and a low of Rs 171.00 in October 2026.

stories.title: Leeds researchers study urban heat in Pune
stories.summary: Researchers from the University of Leeds are collaborating with partners in Pune to study the impact of urban heat on marginalised communities. The project, involving Dr Bhanuben Nanavati College of Architecture and Barefoot Story, aims to identify sustainable adaptation strategies for residents living in informal settlements.

stories.title: IGBC summit discusses climate-resilient urban development
stories.summary: The CII Indian Green Building Council hosted the Green Bengal Summit 2026 in Kolkata to address climate-resilient urban development. Participants discussed sustainable urbanisation, resource efficiency and Net Zero pathways. State ministers emphasised the necessity of these measures for the region's future growth and infrastructure planning.

stories.title: India expands climate risk mapping and planning
stories.summary: India is increasing its climate and environmental data collection through institutions and GIS-based master planning. By August 2026, 23 states and 64 cities had prepared Heat Action Plans. The government is also investing in urban flood risk management to strengthen statutory planning and disaster response.

stories.title: Dar es Salaam faces infrastructure pressure from rainfall
stories.summary: Authorities in Dar es Salaam are inspecting drainage channels and bridges to mitigate flooding risks during the rainy season. With El Niño weather patterns expected, the city is identifying vulnerable areas and warning residents against obstructing waterways to protect roads and infrastructure from further damage.

stories.title: Indian smart cities deploy tech to monitor air quality
stories.summary: Indian cities are using IoT sensors, artificial intelligence and satellite monitoring to track air pollution sources like vehicle emissions and waste burning. These technologies aim to identify hotspots and enable authorities to adjust workflows under the National Clean Air Programme to improve local air quality.

stories.title: Bengaluru urged to adopt process-driven urban planning
stories.summary: Bengaluru faces ongoing crises in water, housing and mobility that require a unified vision rather than individual projects. Experts argue that the city needs to move beyond piecemeal fixes toward a co-developed, process-driven framework to improve liveability and ecological sustainability for its residents.

stories.title: Dr Khurshid Nadeem calls for urban planning reforms
stories.summary: During a visit to the Abbottabad Press Club, Dr Khurshid Ahmed Nadeem highlighted the link between unplanned urban growth and civic traffic problems. He advocated for urban planning, social harmony and peaceful conflict resolution as essential components for building an ideal society.

stories.title: Cyclone Akvan highlights coastal vulnerability
stories.summary: Cyclone Akvan has drawn attention to the risks facing India's eastern coastline. While the name is new for 2026, the Bay of Bengal has experienced numerous devastating storms over the last two decades. Researchers are studying how coastal geography and human development influence these powerful weather events.

stories.title: Global review details urban climate vulnerability
stories.summary: A literature synthesis published in City and Built Environment documents how rapid population growth and infrastructure choices dictate a city's ability to recover from climate extremes. The review, led by A. A. Akinsanola, notes that cities are both victims of and major contributors to global climate change.

stories.title: Panaji mobility plan faces gridlock
stories.summary: Residents of Panaji report increasing difficulty navigating the city, with ambulances and daily commuters frequently stuck in traffic. A smart city blueprint intended to provide relief has been shelved, leaving locals to avoid evening travel as gridlock becomes a predictable feature of the capital.

stories.title: Panaji plans second smart road project
stories.summary: Imagine Panaji Smart City Development Ltd plans to develop a 1.4 km smart road along the Rua de Ourem creek. The Rs 38.2 crore project includes pavement redevelopment and new utility ducts. The work is expected to take over a year and may disrupt local traffic flow.

stories.title: LA evaluates transit performance after World Cup
stories.summary: Los Angeles is reviewing the performance of its transportation network during the World Cup to prepare for the 2028 Olympics. City leaders are assessing whether the systems used during the recent surge in demand can be scaled into a more resilient permanent infrastructure.

stories.title: Los Angeles adds solar street lights
stories.summary: The city of Los Angeles has installed over 1,000 FLT solar street lights. The project is part of a broader municipal effort to upgrade urban infrastructure with sustainable technology.

stories.title: US cities face rising temperatures
stories.summary: All 50 of the largest cities in the United States have become hotter over the past 50 years due to climate change and the urban heat island effect. With over 260 million Americans living in urban areas, rising temperatures are increasing the risk of medical emergencies.

stories.title: American Forests works to close tree canopy gaps
stories.summary: American Forests is partnering with cities like Boynton Beach to address extreme heat by expanding tree canopies. The organisation notes that extreme heat causes more deaths in the United States annually than any other climate disaster, a trend expected to increase significantly by 2050.

stories.title: Trees Atlanta works to maintain urban canopy
stories.summary: Trees Atlanta is planting native species and removing invasive plants to support the city's green spaces. The organization says native trees are essential because the local ecosystem has evolved alongside them. The effort aims to provide food and shelter for wildlife as the city continues to expand.

stories.title: Volunteers work to keep Atlanta's tree canopy green - CBS News
Autodesk and Neilsoft open Pune centre for BIM
stories.summary: Autodesk and Neilsoft have partnered to establish a Centre of Excellence in Pune, focusing on Building Information Modelling and digital twin technology. The facility aims to help businesses adopt cloud-based workflows across the building lifecycle. The centre is located at Neilsoft's headquarters.

stories.title: Autodesk and Neilsoft launch AECO centre in India
stories.summary: Autodesk and Neilsoft have announced a strategic partnership to establish a BIM and digital twin Centre of Excellence in Pune. The collaboration combines Autodesk's industry cloud platform with Neilsoft's delivery expertise to accelerate digital transformation for architecture, engineering, construction and operations clients across the APAC region.

stories.title: DevX launches PropTech accelerator
stories.summary: DevX has launched RE:FRAME, a PropTech accelerator in partnership with Inc42. Ten startups will be selected for the first cohort, with the top five pitching for a share of a 15 crore investment pool. Much of India's real estate sector still relies on spreadsheets and broker networks.

stories.title: AI startups target land records and road repairs
stories.summary: Indian AI startups are addressing fragmented land records and deteriorating road infrastructure. Companies like Landeed are aggregating data to assist with title verification, while others map road damage for authorities. The shift marks a move from pilot projects to everyday civic work in urban governance.

stories.title: Nemetschek signs South Korean university partnership
stories.summary: Nemetschek has signed a three-year agreement with Kyung Hee University, its first academic partnership in South Korea. The deal provides students and faculty access to six construction software tools. The collaboration includes curriculum input and training to prepare engineers for the adoption of building information modelling.

stories.title: One Technology Japan buys 75% of Vietnam's NexConstruct to boost BIM, AI - Dealroom
Terabase launches AI construction execution system
stories.summary: Terabase Energy has released an AI construction execution system for utility-scale solar and wind projects. The software includes an interactive AI agent and a map-first interface to track planned versus installed work. The company says it is defining a new category for the renewable energy industry.

stories.title: Construction software adoption grows in India
stories.summary: The Indian construction industry is increasingly adopting digital technologies to manage complex infrastructure projects. Software tools are being used to coordinate activities and maintain control over budgets and timelines. Builders and engineers are seeking systems to improve project planning, execution and monitoring throughout 2027.

stories.title: Demand for construction consulting rises in India
stories.summary: India's infrastructure sector is driving demand for specialized construction consulting firms. These companies provide engineering knowledge and financial assessments for projects ranging from metro rail networks to smart cities. The increasing scale and technical complexity of developments have necessitated professional planning and design coordination.

stories.title: CAD software remains essential for Indian engineering
stories.summary: Computer-Aided Design software continues to be a standard tool for engineering, architecture and manufacturing in India. The technology allows professionals to create technical drawings and three-dimensional models. It is used for tasks ranging from designing automobile components to planning large-scale residential and commercial infrastructure projects.

stories.title: Ricoh releases 360-degree camera for construction sites
stories.summary: Ricoh has launched the Theta A1, a 360-degree camera designed for construction environments. The device features an IP64-rated dust and water-resistant design and captures 11K photos. It is intended to help project teams document progress and review site details like joints and reference points.

stories.title: Architecture student awarded Charlie Cochrane Medal
stories.summary: Marcelina Janas, a student at the Mackintosh School of Architecture, has received the 2026 Charlie Cochrane Medal for Architecture. Her thesis project, Civic Praxis, was cited for its ambition and ethical responsibility. The award was presented at a ceremony at the City Chambers in November.

stories.title: Kennesaw State students present research findings
stories.summary: Kennesaw State University students are presenting research at the Fall Symposium of Student Scholars. Topics include the use of artificial intelligence in farming and the intersection of architecture and film. The event is hosted each semester by the Office of Undergraduate Research.

stories.title: Situating Architecture Lecture Series 2026-27 - UCL | University College London
Architecture school recovers 1974 protest footage
stories.summary: The School of Architecture has published a nine-minute film from 1974 documenting the first anniversary of the Polytechnic uprising. The footage was recovered from reels stored in a building basement and restored in collaboration with the Greek public broadcaster. It features performances by several prominent Greek musicians.

stories.title: MIT engineering faculty receive summer awards
stories.summary: Faculty and staff at the MIT School of Engineering were recognized with various awards during summer 2026. Among the recipients, Faez Ahmed received a 2025 Air Force Office of Scientific Research Young Investigator Program Award. The grant provides up to 450,000 dollars over three years.

stories.title: Jantar Mantar is no longer a protest site
stories.summary: Jantar Mantar was built nearly 300 years ago as an instrument to measure the heavens and produce scientific knowledge. While often recognised as a hub for public demonstrations, the site was officially denotified as a protest location on 11 October 2026. The heavens remain unaffected.

stories.title: India and Canada trade relations remain steady
stories.summary: Between 2023 and 2024, diplomatic ties between India and Canada faced public acrimony and a near-freeze in high-level engagement. Despite the political friction, trade continued to flow and pension funds maintained their investments. The commercial relationship held steady while the political one did not.

stories.title: India Biennale 2026 returns to Delhi
stories.summary: The second edition of the India Biennale, themed around reconnecting in an age of distraction, will run for 108 days starting this December. Presented by the Ministry of Culture, the event will host exhibitions and workshops across the capital's historic monuments, museums, and public gardens.
